entities.summary:
Imran, a revered figure in Abrahamic traditions, particularly Islam, flourished in Jerusalem during the late Second Temple period (roughly 1st century BCE to 1st century CE). As the father of Mary (Maryam) and grandfather of Jesus ('Isa), his significance is primarily derived from his lineage and his family's profound connection to the spiritual and physical fabric of the Jerusalem Temple. While not extensively detailed in canonical biblical texts, Islamic tradition portrays him as a righteous leader and a prominent member of a priestly family, embodying piety and dedication within the religious community of his era.

His life, as understood through later religious narratives, centered on devout service and the upbringing of his daughter, Mary. Imran and his wife, Hannah (or Anna in Christian tradition), are depicted as a pious couple who, despite advanced age, prayed for a child and vowed to dedicate any offspring to God's service within the Temple. This vow led to Mary's unique upbringing under the care of Temple priests, most notably Zechariah, in a dedicated chamber within the sacred precincts. The association with 'architects & engineers' might metaphorically refer to his role in upholding the spiritual 'architecture' of the community or, more literally, to a family lineage involved in the maintenance or patronage of the Temple's physical structures, a common role for prominent priestly families.
